news.title: Max Financial Services Limited Just Missed Earnings - But Analysts Have Updated Their Models
news.body: As you might know, Max Financial Services Limited ( NSE:MFSL ) last week released its latest yearly, and things did not...

news.title: Full year 2026 earnings: EPS and revenues miss analyst expectations
news.body: Full year 2026 results: EPS: ₹2.42 (down from ₹9.63 in FY 2025). Revenue: ₹477.0b (up 2.6% from FY 2025). Net income: ₹828.5m (down 75% from FY 2025). Profit margin: 0.2% (down from 0.7% in FY 2025). The decrease in margin was driven by higher expenses. Revenue missed analyst estimates by 8.4%. Earnings per share (EPS) also missed analyst estimates by 79%. Revenue is forecast to grow 17% p.a. on average during the next 3 years, compared to a 11% growth forecast for the Insurance industry in India. Over the last 3 years on average, earnings per share has fallen by 36% per year but the company’s share price has increased by 34% per year, which means it is well ahead of earnings.

news.title: MFSL: Planned Capital Raise For Subsidiary Will Support 2026 Outlook
news.body: Analysts have trimmed their price target for Max Financial Services slightly from ₹2,055.48 to ₹2,050.56, citing updated assumptions around discount rates, revenue growth, profit margins, and future P/E levels. What's in the News A board meeting is scheduled for March 12, 2026, to consider, evaluate, and approve raising further capital to meet the funding requirements of material subsidiary Axis Max Life Insurance Limited, including the potential issuance of equity shares and other eligible securities through various modes (Key Developments).

news.title: MFSL: Planned Amalgamation Will Support 2026 Outlook
news.body: Analysts have kept their price target for Max Financial Services steady at about ₹2,055, citing largely unchanged fair value assumptions along with only small adjustments to revenue growth, profit margin and future P/E expectations. What's in the News Board meeting on Jan 28, 2026, to discuss and provide in principle approval for a potential amalgamation between Max Financial Services and its subsidiary Axis Max Life Insurance Limited (AMLI) (company event filing).

news.title: Consensus EPS estimates fall by 13%
news.body: The consensus outlook for fiscal year 2026 has been updated. 2026 EPS estimate fell from ₹12.84 to ₹11.18 per share. Revenue forecast steady at ₹519.4b. Net income forecast to grow 324% next year vs 19% growth forecast for Insurance industry in India. Consensus price target up from ₹1,928 to ₹2,081. Share price rose 5.9% to ₹1,836 over the past week.

news.title: Price target increased by 8.0% to ₹2,081
news.body: Up from ₹1,928, the current price target is an average from 25 analysts. New target price is 14% above last closing price of ₹1,825. Stock is up 73% over the past year. The company is forecast to post earnings per share of ₹11.18 for next year compared to ₹9.63 last year.

news.title: New minor risk - Profit margin trend
news.body: The company's profit margins are lower than last year and have reduced by more than 30%. Net profit margin: 0.3% Last year net profit margin: 0.5% This is considered a minor risk. A large drop in profit margin could indicate the company does not have strong competitive advantages or it is yet to establish itself and its core business. Even if it is a well established business, this may make it a much riskier investment than one that has a combination of proven competitive advantages and a stable or growing profit margin. This is currently the only risk that has been identified for the company.

news.title: Third quarter 2026 earnings released: EPS: ₹1.07 (vs ₹1.62 in 3Q 2025)
news.body: Third quarter 2026 results: EPS: ₹1.07 (down from ₹1.62 in 3Q 2025). Revenue: ₹142.7b (up 60% from 3Q 2025). Net income: ₹365.5m (down 35% from 3Q 2025). Profit margin: 0.3% (down from 0.6% in 3Q 2025). The decrease in margin was driven by higher expenses. Revenue is forecast to grow 15% p.a. on average during the next 3 years, compared to a 9.8% growth forecast for the Insurance industry in India. Over the last 3 years on average, earnings per share has fallen by 23% per year but the company’s share price has increased by 35% per year, which means it is well ahead of earnings.
